drafted_from: tool:update-a-servers-tls-owner's row in tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/tool-rows.json, do-work/renew-a-tls-certificate.mjs, do-work/tls-host-owner.py and the tests in test/
start_here: Say to your AI: "Update the certificate owner and its layout on my server at 192.0.2.34 after the layout changed." It runs tool:update-a-servers-tls-owner, which rewrites only the owner and its layout file and installs nothing.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it takes one server's facts as its input and answers what that server's certificate owner reports.
instructions: 1. Gather the server's facts: its public name, IPv4 address, SSH port, the administrator you sign in as, its pinned key ("<address> ssh-ed25519 <key>") and its layout (host: owner path, state folder, downloads folder, ingress, receptionist). The README in tools/renew-a-tls-certificate/ shows a made-up one.

2. Say to your AI the sentence in start_here. It calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:update-a-servers-tls-owner and that input (the worked example shows one). The door mounts your server administration key for the run; you paste no key.
3. Read what comes back: {"tls_owner_installed": true}. An {"error": ...} or a thrown message names what to change (for example the layout or the pinned key was refused).

4. The layout goes first, then the owner, each written whole and moved into place; nothing is restarted, so run tool:read-a-servers-tls-certificate afterwards if you want to confirm the server still answers.
